# COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE REPORT
**Feature:** Rewards earning rules display to reduce support tickets

---

## COMPETITORS:

### 1. OneCard | Rewards Transparency [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Explicitly addresses reward rate confusion through app-based explanations.

**What they built:** OneCard displays reward rates ranging from 0.2% to 2% directly in their app interface, with the specific rate shown for each transaction category. The app shows "Simple Rewards" messaging to reduce confusion about variable cashback rates across different merchant categories.

**One key point:** Despite transparency efforts, users still report confusion about why certain transactions earn different rates, suggesting display alone doesn't fully solve the problem.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://cardmaven.in/onecard-review-ltf-metal-credit-card-in-india/ and https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/

---

### 2. Scapia | Rewards Communication [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Travel-focused card with variable rewards that requires clear earning rule communication.

**What they built:** Scapia displays rewards earning on card spends with partner-specific rates shown upfront on their website and app. They use visual logos of partner merchants to communicate where higher rewards apply, making earning rules more intuitive through brand recognition rather than text explanations.

**One key point:** Their approach focuses on pre-transaction clarity (showing rates before spending) rather than post-transaction explanations.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from marketing materials)

**Source:** https://www.scapia.cards/

---

### 3. Slice | UPI Cashback Simplicity [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Built around "simple 1% UPI cashback" messaging to eliminate confusion entirely.

**What they built:** Slice uses a flat 1% cashback structure specifically to avoid the complexity of variable rates and earning rule explanations. Their Reddit reviews highlight that users appreciate the simplicity and predictability, with no need for post-transaction explanations because the rate is always the same.

**One key point:** They solved the support ticket problem by eliminating variable rates entirely rather than explaining them better.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

---

### 4. American Express Platinum | Premium Rewards Clarity [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Global best practice for high-value cardholders who demand transparency on complex rewards.

**What they built:** Amex provides detailed earning rule breakdowns in account statements and app notifications, with specific callouts for bonus categories and exclusions. Their 'Global Dining Credit' and other benefits come with clear terms displayed at point of enrollment and in monthly summaries.

**One key point:** Premium positioning allows them to invest in detailed, personalized explanations that match their high-touch service model.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from global practices document)

**Source:** https://evessio.s3.amazonaws.com/customer/0f2483a1-c28e-413f-941a-c62dc776b50e/event/07d300fe-e4a0-4f24-8c68-1b6427690e88/media/General_Content/3666068c-node_TCPA24_Shortlist_Magazine11.pdf

---

### 5. Revolut | Transaction-Level Transparency [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Global neobank known for real-time transaction notifications with contextual information.

**What they built:** Revolut's app shows instant notifications for every transaction with contextual details including fees, exchange rates, and applicable benefits. Their 2023 redesign (Revolut 10) emphasized real-time clarity on all financial actions, making every transaction self-explanatory at the moment it occurs.

**One key point:** They treat transparency as a core product differentiator, not just a support cost reduction tool.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from annual report)

**Source:** https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

---

## WHITESPACE SIGNAL:

**FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY:** No Indian digital-first card has built proactive, AI-driven earning rule explanations that predict user confusion before support contact—all current solutions are either reactive displays or simplified flat rates.

---

## WHAT REAL USERS SAY:

**Observation 1:** OneCard users on Reddit report that despite in-app reward rate displays, they still don't understand "why certain transactions earn different rates," indicating that showing rates isn't the same as explaining the logic behind them.

**Source:** https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/ (user feedback section)

**Observation 2:** Slice credit card users explicitly praise the "simple 1% UPI cashback" because it eliminates confusion entirely—one Reddit reviewer called it "refreshingly straightforward" compared to variable rate cards.

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

**Observation 3:** No community discussions found specifically about post-transaction earning rule explanations or support ticket reduction features in current sources.

---

## GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY:

**Global neobank approach (Revolut, Monzo):** Leading digital banks treat transaction transparency as a core product feature, not an afterthought. Revolut's 2023 redesign prioritized real-time contextual information for every financial action, making transactions self-explanatory at the moment they occur. Monzo uses plain-language notifications that explain fees and benefits instantly.

**What works:** Proactive, real-time explanations at the moment of transaction (not buried in FAQs), visual design that highlights key information, and plain language that avoids financial jargon.

**Why it works:** Users don't have to remember rules or search for information—the app anticipates their questions and answers them immediately, building trust through transparency.

**Source:** https://www.fintechfutures.com/press-releases/global-neobanks-industry-report-2024-monzo-revolut-nubank-and-kakaobank-the-digital-challenger-banks and https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

---

## RBI COMPLIANCE:

Not found in current sources. No specific RBI mandate identified for rewards earning rule disclosure beyond standard credit card terms and conditions requirements.

---

## DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES:

### Angle 1: Zero-UI Predictive Silence
**What to build:** Automatically detect which transactions will trigger user confusion (based on ML patterns from past support tickets) and send proactive push notifications explaining the cashback rate before the user even wonders.

**Strategic logic:** This is a defensive play—eliminate support tickets by predicting and preventing confusion rather than explaining after the fact, positioning PIXEL as the "card that reads your mind."

**RBI compliance:** No additional compliance burden; standard transaction notification rules apply.

**Build complexity:** High (requires ML model training on support ticket data, real-time transaction scoring, and notification orchestration)

**Ops impact:** Requires initial tagging of historical support tickets to train the model, then minimal ongoing ops once the system learns patterns.

---

### Angle 2: Gamified Earning Mastery
**What to build:** Create an in-app "Rewards Academy" where users unlock achievement badges for understanding different earning rules, with interactive quizzes and visual progress tracking that turns confusion into engagement.

**Strategic logic:** This is an offensive play—transform a support cost center into a retention and engagement driver by making learning about rewards fun, targeting users who want to optimize their spending.

**RBI compliance:** No compliance issues; purely educational content within the app.

**Build complexity:** Medium (requires content creation, gamification mechanics, and progress tracking, but no complex backend logic)

**Ops impact:** Requires content team to create and maintain educational modules, plus periodic updates when reward rules change.

---

### Angle 3: Intelligent Contextual Tooltips
**What to build:** Add smart, context-aware tooltips in transaction history that appear only when the cashback rate differs from the user's typical pattern, with one-tap explanations that reference the specific merchant category and applicable rule.

**Strategic logic:** This is a transactional play—solve the immediate problem at the exact moment of confusion with minimal UI intrusion, keeping the core experience clean while providing help exactly when needed.

**RBI compliance:** No additional compliance requirements; enhances existing transaction display.

**Build complexity:** Low (requires rule engine to match transactions to earning rules and conditional UI display logic)

**Ops impact:** Requires one-time mapping of merchant categories to earning rules, then automated updates when rules change.

---

## RECOMMENDED ANGLE:

**Which angle:** Intelligent Contextual Tooltips

**Why now:** PIXEL is in early stage and needs quick wins that demonstrably reduce support tickets without requiring ML infrastructure or content teams—this angle delivers immediate impact with existing engineering capabilities and can be shipped in 4-6 weeks.

**Why not the others:**
- **Zero-UI Predictive Silence:** Requires 6+ months of support ticket data to train ML models effectively, and PIXEL may not have sufficient historical data yet to build accurate prediction models.
- **Gamified Earning Mastery:** Solves engagement but doesn't directly address the support ticket problem—users who are confused won't voluntarily enter a "Rewards Academy," and this requires ongoing content operations that PIXEL may not have capacity for.

---

## OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium

**Reason:** Strong signal that variable reward rates cause user confusion across multiple digital-first cards, but limited evidence of competitors building sophisticated post-transaction explanation features. The 800 monthly support tickets suggest real pain, but no direct user research found in sources to validate specific solution approaches.

---

## SUMMARY:

- Digital-first cards show rates but don't explain earning logic causing continued user confusion
- Slice eliminated confusion with flat rates while OneCard still faces support questions despite transparency
- Medium confidence due to limited evidence of post-transaction explanation features in market
